items.topic: The model moved before the rain
coherentNarrative: At the beginning of the afternoon, Aditi placed her clay model on an outdoor exhibition table.
While checking that table, she noticed that dark clouds were approaching.
Because of the approaching clouds, she asked the organiser whether the model could be moved indoors.
After hearing her request, the organiser showed her a suitable indoor display space.
With that space confirmed, two adults helped her move the fragile model safely.
Once the model was inside, Aditi put a direction sign on the now-empty outdoor table.
Following the sign, the first visitors reached the indoor display just as rain began.
After the visitors arrived, Aditi explained how changing the arrangement had protected the exhibition.

coherentNarrative: One morning, Salim arranged to meet his cousin beneath the village clock at noon.
On reaching the clock before the agreed time, he noticed that its hands had stopped.
This discovery made him check the time on the community office clock nearby.
After checking, he returned to the meeting place and waited rather than assuming his cousin was late.
A few minutes into his wait, his cousin arrived and pointed at the motionless hands.
Salim then explained that he had already checked the time at the office.
Having settled the confusion, the cousins reported the faulty clock to the responsible caretaker.
After making that report, they continued to their appointment together.

items.topic: The rehearsal with a missing puppet
coherentNarrative: Before a children’s performance, the drama group discovered that its largest puppet had been damaged.
On seeing the damage, the group leader told the teacher that the planned opening could not proceed normally.
In response, the teacher asked the performers to suggest an alternative using their remaining props.
Following that invitation, one pupil proposed introducing the missing character through narration.
After the group accepted this idea, they rehearsed the changed opening together.
Once the rehearsal was complete, the leader explained the change to the person operating the sound.
With everyone informed, the performers presented their revised opening to the audience.
When the performance ended, they thanked one another for adapting without blaming a single member.

items.topic: The loose pages of a local history
coherentNarrative: One afternoon, a librarian opened an old local-history book and found several loose pages.
After noticing the damage, she removed the book from ordinary lending to prevent further loss.
With the book protected, she checked its page numbers and made a record of the loose sections.
Using that record, she asked a suitably experienced book conservator for advice.
After examining the recorded damage, the conservator proposed an appropriate repair.
Once the library approved the proposal, the conservator carried out the agreed work.
Following the repair, the librarian checked the book against her earlier record.
After completing that check, she returned it to use under the recommended handling conditions.

coherentNarrative: Before beginning a woven wall hanging, apprentice Rima copied a pattern onto squared paper.
While counting the copied rows, she found that the two sides did not match.
This mismatch led her to compare the copy with the original design.
After that comparison, she discovered one row that she had accidentally left out.
Having found the omission, she corrected the paper pattern before cutting any thread.
Once the correction was complete, her instructor checked the revised drawing.
With the instructor’s confirmation, Rima began weaving from the corrected pattern.
After finishing the first section, she was glad that the mistake had been found before work began.

coherentNarrative: At the first rehearsal, a music group tried a new piece at a very fast tempo.
As the piece continued, several players struggled to keep their parts together.
Noticing that difficulty, the conductor stopped the rehearsal and invited comments.
In response, one player asked whether they could practise the difficult passage more slowly.
After agreeing to the request, the conductor chose a slower starting tempo.
At that slower tempo, the group worked through the passage until the entries became clearer.
Once the entries were secure, they gradually increased the pace under the conductor’s direction.
At the end of the rehearsal, the players discussed how the slower practice had helped them listen.

coherentNarrative: Before editing a fictional school podcast, Kanta opened the file from the previous day’s interview.
On playing the file, she discovered that no voice could be heard.
Because the file was silent, she checked the recorder’s backup folder before doing anything else.
After finding a usable backup there, she listened to confirm that the whole agreed interview was present.
With the recording confirmed, she checked the speaker’s permission for the proposed classroom use.
Once the permission was confirmed too, she selected a short extract that represented the account fairly.
After editing that extract, she sent it to the speaker for the agreed review.
Only after receiving the review did she prepare the final classroom version.

coherentNarrative: Before a supervised group walk, the adult leader checked the current conditions and local advice.
That check revealed poor visibility on the route the group had planned to use.
Because of the poor visibility, the leader postponed the outdoor walk before anyone set out.
After announcing the postponement, she contacted the participants through the agreed channels.
Once the messages were sent, she arranged an indoor map-reading session for those already present.
During that session, participants compared the planned route with a map of the area.
After comparing the routes, they discussed why a timetable should not overrule a safety decision.
At the close of the session, the leader said a new walk would require fresh checks and arrangements.

coherentNarrative: At the start of an orchard collection day, a worker checked the scales with the approved reference weight.
The check showed that the scales were not giving the expected reading.
On finding this error, the worker stopped using them and informed the supervisor.
After receiving the report, the supervisor arranged a suitable checked replacement.
Once the replacement arrived, authorised staff confirmed that it was ready for use.
With the replacement confirmed, the team resumed weighing the collected fruit.
After the collection, the supervisor attached a clear fault notice to the original scales.
Following that notice, the faulty equipment remained out of use pending qualified attention.

coherentNarrative: Before borrowing a backdrop, a youth theatre group asked its owner about the permitted use.
In reply, the owner allowed one indoor performance but excluded painting or cutting the fabric.
After receiving those conditions, the group planned a set that left the borrowed backdrop unchanged.
With the set plan agreed, the owner and organiser recorded the backdrop’s condition before collection.
Once the backdrop reached the venue, authorised adults installed it according to the approved plan.
After the performance, the group arranged its careful removal and return.
On its return, the owner compared its condition with the record made before the loan.
After completing that comparison, both sides confirmed that the agreed borrowing period had ended.
